sentences.text: This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. by petitioner/accused No.1 to enlarge him on bail in Crime No.14/2023 of Anugondanahalli Police Station, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B, read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

2. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent- State and perused the material on record.
3.

The case of prosecution is that, marriage of deceased-Pallavi M.R., daughter of complainant was performed with petitioner/accused No.1 on 24/25.05.2022 at Sri.Shubhameru Kalyana Mantapa,
Chikka Thirupathi, Malur Taluk, Kolar District.
At the time of marriage cash of Rs.2,00,000/- was given to the bridegroom and golden ornaments were given to the bride as well as the bride groom.

After about two months, petitioner and his parents i.e., accused Nos.2 and 3, started subjecting the NC: 2023:KHC:20436 deceased to physical and mental torture demanding her to bring a sum of Rs.50,000/-.
As per their demand, sum of Rs.50,000/-, was paid to them.
Inspite of that accused were subjecting the deceased to physical and mental torture.
Unable to tolerate the said torture, to put an end to her life, Pallavi consumed insecticide on 31.01.2023 at about 9.00 am.

She was immediately shifted to hospital for treatment, however, she died on 02.02.2023 at about 8.25 am.
4.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the petitioner is working as a teacher in a private school and at no point of time he has demanded dowry.
He submits that the entire marriage expenses are met by the family of the petitioner.
He submits that petitioner was not present in the house at the time of incident and his mother who was present, shifted the victim to hospital for treatment.
He submits that accused Nos.2 and 3 i.e., parents of the petitioner herein have been enlarged on bail.
He submits that petitioner is ready NC: 2023:KHC:20436 and willing to abide by any conditions and therefore, seeks to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader has contended that the petitioner has subjected the deceased to cruelty, making unlawful demands and therefore, she has committed suicide.
Hence, he prays to reject the petition.

sentences.text: 6. It is not in dispute that deceased-Pallavi committed suicide within seven years of her marriage.

The allegations are that at the time of marriage, accused persons received dowry in the form of cash and gold and subsequent to the marriage, they have demanded additional dowry and in this connection they were subjecting the deceased to physical and mental torture.
It is further alleged that a sum of Rs.50,000/- was given to the accused and inspite of that, they were torturing the deceased and therefore, she committed suicide.
Deceased has consumed poison in the house of the accused on 31.01.2023 at about 9.00 am.
The statement of C.Ws.14 and 15 shows that accused No.2 i.e., mother-in-law of the deceased requested them to shift the deceased to the hospital for treatment.
Victim was not in a position to talk and immediately they shifted her to one R.K.B.Sanjeevini Hospital.
Thereafter, she was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, for higher treatment.
She died on 02.02.2023.
As per C.W.15- Manjula, petitioner has taken the victim to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, for higher treatment.
8. At this stage, there is no material to show that, petitioner was present in the house and he subjected the deceased to cruelty soon before her death.
Prosecution has to establish its case in a full-fledged trial.
Petitioner was arrested on 09.02.2023.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed.
He is not required for further interrogation.
Accused Nos.2 and 3 are already enlarged on bail by this Court in Crl.P.No.3691/2023 dated NC: 2023:KHC:20436 22.05.2023.
Petitioner has undertaken to furnish sufficient surety to ensure his presence before the trial Court.
In the facts and circumstances, relief sought by the petitioner can be granted, by imposing conditions.

Hence, the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

Petitioner/accused No.1 in Crime No.14/2023 of Anugondanahalli Police Station,
shall be released on bail subject to following conditions:
a) Petitioner shall execute a bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only)
with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
b) Petitioner shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the Investigation Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
c) Petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission of the trial Court.
NC: 2023:KHC:20436 d) Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
e) Petitioner shall appear before the trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.
